chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq, from Isḥāq, from Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

What suffices you for ghusl (ritual bath) and istinjāʾ is that by which you moisten your hand, and whatever other reports run along the same lines; for they are to be understood as indicating sufficiency, while the former reports indicate excellence. However, despite that, the water must necessarily flow over the limbs so that it may be considered washing, even if it is a small amount like oil; for whenever it does not flow, it is not called washing, and that would not be sufficient. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.الْأَعْضَاءِ: the bodily limbs over which water must flow
key_terms.الْإِجْزَاءِ: legal sufficiency; that which fulfills the minimum valid requirement
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl (ritual bath), specifically the act whose validity depends on actual washing
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: superior merit or excellence beyond the minimum sufficiency
key_terms.غَاسِلًا: counted as washing in the legal sense
key_terms.مُجْزِيًا: sufficient and valid for fulfilling the requirement

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of water that suffices for ghusl and wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the minimum amount of water sufficient for ghusl and istinjāʾ, clarifying that reports mentioning very small amounts are understood as indicating sufficiency, while other reports indicate what is more virtuous. It emphasizes that water must actually flow over the limbs for the act to count as washing; mere moisture without flow is not sufficient.
